_about: Building and city standards for Invicta (Jordan, 28 Nov 2026), from US practice: the International Building Code, ADA accessibility guidelines and AASHTO street design. Values are metres (the data files store metric); 'us' keys give the same size in US units for people. atlaslib/fabric.py reads the doors, windows, walls and stairs under 'building'. 'decks' is canon. 'streets', 'blocks', 'street_furniture', 'civil', 'materials' and 'drafting' are recorded for later steps: nothing reads them yet, and no deck layout changes from them without Jordan's OK.
source: Jordan, 28 Nov 2026: door heights (6 ft 8 in standard, 7 ft under 9-10 ft ceilings, 8 ft grand entrances).
Jordan, 28 Nov 2026: modern city standards (streets, building heights, doors, windows, stairs, blocks, street furniture, materials).
Jordan, 28 Nov 2026: real-world blueprint standards (IBC, ADA, AASHTO): drafting, wall assemblies, door and window schedules, millwork, stairs, rails, ramps, street rights-of-way, utilities.
Jordan, 28 Nov 2026: no stairs between decks; only fast elevators and teleport pads, for people and vehicles.
Jordan, 28 Nov 2026: every deck has the Atrium and the Spine Atrium at its centre; deck-to-deck transport for people and ships (teleporters and elevators) is there.

doors.us_single_width: 3 ft 0 in (36 in), the ADA minimum for a commercial door (32 in clear when open)
doors.us_height: 6 ft 8 in (80 in), the US standard door
doors.us_tall_height: 7 ft 0 in, under ceilings of 9 ft or more
doors.us_entrance_height: 8 ft 0 in, grand commercial entrances (also openings between corridors)
doors.us_residential_interior_width: 2 ft 6 in to 2 ft 8 in (homes; not used yet)
doors.us_rough_opening_add: 2 in wider and 2-1/2 in taller than the door, for jambs and shims

windows.us_sill: 3 ft 0 in above the floor (standard 30-36 in)
windows.us_head: 7 ft 0 in above the floor, in line with the tops of doors
windows.us_curtain_wall_grid: 5 ft (high-rise glass walls; not used yet)
windows.us_egress_sill_max: 44 in highest sill for a bedroom escape window
windows.us_egress_open_min: 5.7 sq ft clear opening for a bedroom escape window

stairs.us_riser_max: 7 in (all risers in a flight within 3/8 in of each other)
stairs.us_flight_width_min: 44 in, the commercial egress minimum (36 in in homes, 60 in for big crowds)
stairs.us_headroom: 6 ft 8 in clear above the stair nosings
stairs.us_handrail_height: 34-38 in above the nosings, running 12 in past the top and bottom (not built yet)
stairs.us_guardrail_height: 42 in on commercial landings, balconies and roofs (36 in in homes), gaps under 4 in (not built yet)

building.us_parapet: 3-4 ft wall round a flat roof (not built yet)
building.us_plinth: 6-12 in concrete or stone base where walls meet the ground (not built yet)

walls.us_partition: 4-7/8 in (2x4 studs and two layers of 5/8 in drywall)
walls.us_partition_rated: 6-3/4 in for sound or fire walls (not used yet)
walls.us_exterior: 12 in (range 6-3/4 to 12 in with insulation and cladding)
walls.us_core: 10 in stair and lift core walls (concrete)

structure.us_column_grid: 20 x 20 ft to 30 x 40 ft steel grid (not used yet)
structure.us_elevated_floor_depth: 18-36 in total: concrete on metal deck, steel joists and the services space

ramps.us_rise_per_run_max: 30 in, then a level 5 x 5 ft (1.52 x 1.52 m) landing

millwork.us_counter: 24 in deep base cabinets, 36 in counters
millwork.us_wall_cabinet: 12 in deep, 18 in above the counter (54 in above the floor)

streets.us_traffic_lane: 11.5-12 ft (10 ft on tight residential streets)
streets.us_bike_lane: 5-6 ft, plus a 2 ft (0.6 m) buffer beside traffic
streets.us_crosswalk_width: 10-15 ft, set back 4 ft (1.2 m) from the stop line
streets.us_crown_grade: 2% fall from the centre line to the curbs

blocks.zero_lot_line: downtown shops sit right at the back of the sidewalk

street_furniture.us_streetlight_height: 25-30 ft on avenues; 12-15 ft (3.5-4.5 m) for walkways

materials.load_bearing: heavy materials (stone, brick, concrete) at the base, lighter (glass, metal panels, stucco) higher up; a visible lintel, beam or column over every opening
materials.us_facade_grid: 10 or 15 ft modules, so walls and windows meet cleanly

decks.between_decks: No stairs between decks: they would be far too big. People and vehicles go deck to deck only by fast elevators and teleport pads. Stairs are only inside buildings, between a building's own floors.
decks.spine_atrium: Every deck has an Atrium and the Spine Atrium at its centre (the open shaft through the decks). Deck-to-deck transport for people and ships, by teleporter or elevator, is in the Spine Atrium.

civil.us_right_of_way: local streets 50-60 ft (two 10-11 ft lanes, 8 ft parking, 5 ft sidewalks); avenues 80-100 ft (four 11-12 ft lanes, centre turn lane or median, bike lanes, 8-12 ft sidewalks); boulevards 120-150 ft (six 12 ft lanes, 16-24 ft median, loading, 12-20 ft plazas)
civil.us_curb_return_radius: 15-20 ft at homes, 25-35 ft on truck and bus routes
civil.us_utility_depth: sewer 6-12 ft (0.5-1% fall), storm drain 4-8 ft, water 3-5 ft, power and telecom ducts 24-36 in

scales.plans: 1/4 in = 1 ft (1:50), large buildings 1/8 in = 1 ft (1:100)

drafting.note: Dimension to structural grid lines and rough openings, not paint.
